questions.q: Propene is oxidised with O₂ in aqueous PdCl₂/CuCl₂. The product is:
questions.explain: In the Wacker oxidation the oxygen goes to the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov), so terminal alkenes give methyl ketones. Propanal is the common trap; only ethene gives an aldehyde.

questions.q: In the Wacker process, the function of CuCl₂ is to:
options: Supply the oxygen atom of the carbonyl group
Coordinate the alkene as a π-complex
Add chloride to the alkene to form a chlorohydrin
questions.explain: PdCl₂ is reduced to Pd metal as it oxidises the alkene; CuCl₂ turns Pd(0) back into Pd(II) and becomes CuCl, which O₂ re-oxidises. So both metals are catalytic and only the alkene and O₂ are consumed.

questions.q: In the Wacker oxidation of ethene to acetaldehyde, the oxygen atom of the C=O group comes from:
questions.explain: Water attacks the palladium-bound alkene (hydroxypalladation), so it supplies the carbonyl oxygen. O₂ is only the final oxidant that regenerates the copper and palladium catalysts.

questions.q: Ethene oxidised by the Wacker process in D₂O gives CH₃CHO containing no deuterium. This result rules out:
options: A free enol intermediate that tautomerises to the aldehyde
questions.explain: If a free enol CH₂=CHOH tautomerised in D₂O, deuterium would end up on carbon. Its absence shows that the C=O forms on palladium by hydride shifts, so no keto–enol step is involved even though some notes draw one.
